open_questions: Which sector/aperture combination produces the variable depths (SPOC vs SPOC 2-min vs true astrophysical variability)?
Is the phase-0.7489 secondary a true eclipse at half-orbit or a brightness bump that mimics one (secondary_over_bump 0.931)?
Gaia RV (rv_amplitude 2.177 km/s, rv_gof 1.797) and RUWE 1.151 suggest binarity - confirm with high-resolution spectroscopy
dossier.public_summary: The 13.8-day 1.2-Earth dip is flat-bottomed but appears strongly at only one or two transits and vanishes in later sectors, varies by over threefold, lasts about 30% longer than expected, and shows a second eclipse at half phase about 40% as deep as the primary. Together the variable depths, long duration and stellar eclipses favour either a false alarm from a few bad events or a close stellar binary on the target, not a stable planet. Residual confirmation of a planet would need consistent identical transits in future TESS sectors and spectroscopy ruling out binarity.

reasons.why: Depth is not steady; it really changes by ~372% across sectors and within the 2-min pipeline including a deep outlier in sector 29 and a non-detection in sector 69, inconsistent with a single planet depth.
